run.procedureSummary: Read the write-up (metallurgy.md) and ran five cycles. In each cycle the five moves run in this order, and each move finishes across all six crucibles before the next starts. (1) Charge: add that cycle's charge-sheet row to each crucible. Volume is not checked during charging. (2) Overflow: walk crucibles 1 to 6. Anything above a crucible's working volume moves into the next crucible before that one is checked, so overflow can chain down the line. Overflow from crucible 6 goes to slag. (3) Temperature: check each crucible's melt after overflow against its current state. A BASE crucible with melt at or above its upper mark becomes SUPERHEATED. A SUPERHEATED crucible with melt at or below its lower mark becomes BASE. Otherwise the state stays the same. Every change is logged. (4) Bleed: take a snapshot of all six amounts and work out every transfer from that snapshot, then apply them all at once. A BASE crucible loses floor(q/4) to slag. A SUPERHEATED crucible sends floor(q/2) to the crucible before it, and crucible 1's half goes to slag. A crucible can end the bleed above its volume. That excess stays until the next cycle's overflow, and after cycle 5 it remains. (5) Emergency tap: total the line after the bleed. If the total is strictly greater than 38, remove floor(q/2) from every crucible to slag, so each crucible keeps ceil(q/2), and log the cycle. The slag tally is the sum of overflow from crucible 6, BASE skims, crucible 1's bleed half and tap removals.

openPoints.point: How halving rounds in the emergency tap when a crucible holds an odd amount
openPoints.assumption: The amount removed is rounded down (floor(q/2) goes to slag), so the crucible keeps ceil(q/2). This matches the bleed, where the amount moved is rounded down.

openPoints.point: How the bleed rounds a quarter or a half
openPoints.assumption: The amount skimmed or sent is rounded down: floor(q/4) for BASE and floor(q/2) for SUPERHEATED.
Only in the temperature move, using melt after overflow. Changes in melt from the bleed or the tap do not change a state until the next cycle's temperature move.

openPoints.point: What 'read all six before touching any' means for the bleed
openPoints.assumption: All transfers are worked out from the amounts before the bleed. Melt a crucible receives from the next crucible down the line is not bled again in the same cycle.

openPoints.point: A tap total exactly equal to 38
openPoints.assumption: No tap, because the rule says strictly over. This came up in cycle 3, where the total was exactly 38.

openPoints.point: Melt above volume after the bleed in cycle 5
openPoints.assumption: It stays where it is. In fact no crucible was above volume after the cycle 5 tap.
